 Judgment

This appeal is arising out of the Judgment and award passed in MVC No.2036/2015 dated 10.10.2017 by the IX Addl. District and Sessions Judge and Addl. MACT., Belagavi (hereinafter for short 'Tribunal').

entities.text: IX Addl. District and Sessions Judge and Addl. MACT., Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 06.10.2014 at about 6.45 p.m., near the bus stop at Balekundri K.H. village when the appellant/claimant was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-22/EN-2941, a Mahendra Max Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA-39/2621 driven by it's driver came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner and thereby caused injuries to him.

The petitioner was admitted as inpatient at Vijaya Hospital,
Belagavi.
Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant-claimant before the Tribunal in MVC No.2036/2015 claiming for compensation against the respondents.

3. The Tribunal after appreciating the material on record and evidence placed before it, allowed the claim petition in part and granted compensation of Rs.2,27,898/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The tribunal held respondent No.2-Insurance company liable to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the said award appellant/claimant has preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

4. We have heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant/claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 insurance company and perused the materials on record, including the trial court record.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the Tribunal totally erred while awarding the compensation by holding that the accident took place due to the fault/negligent driving on the part of the drivers of both the vehicles i.e. offending vehicle and also by the petitioner/appellant and thereby the contribution to the accident is considered at the ratio of 75 %
and 25% respectively.

The said conclusion was arrived by the Tribunal only for the reason that the claimant/appellant was riding the motorcycle without having driving license as on the date of accident and since, the accident was caused due to head on collusion between two vehicles and in the absence of driving license of the appellant/claimant, it cannot be said that the appellant has also contributed to the accident to some extent.
The learned counsel submits that the said findings of the Tribunal cannot be sustained.
He relied the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sri.Dinesh Kumar J. @ Dinesh J. Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd., and others.

sentences.text: The counsel further contended that the Tribunal also erred while considering the disability caused to the petitioner due to the accident.

The Doctor who was examined as PW.2 before the Tribunal categorically stated that the claimant has got permanent physical disability to an extent of 40% to the right lower limb and to an extent of 20% to right hand, to that effect he has also issued a certificate as per Ex.P.12.

But, the Tribunal even after arriving at the conclusion that total functional disability of the body could be considered as 35% but loss of earning capacity is considered at 12%.
The said finding of the Tribunal is unacceptable as it is without any basis.

He relied the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sri.Anthony alias Anthony Swamy Vs. The Managing Director,
KSRTC, in Civil Appeal No.2551/2020 (arising out of SLP(Civil) No.1738/2018).

sentences.text: 7. The counsel for the appellant would further contend that the Tribunal also erred in taking the notional income of the appellant at Rs.7,000/- per month.
As per Lok- adalath chart, for the accident of the year-2014, notional income is Rs.7,500/- per month.
Hence, learned counsel for appellant prays to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2- Insurance Company vehemently contended that the award passed by the Tribunal does not call for any interference and the same is based on the evidence available on record.

According to the learned counsel, the Tribunal has rightly considered fact that the accident took place due to the fault on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and also by the petitioner since the accident was due to head on collusion between two vehicles and the appellant being the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-22/2941 contributed towards the accident since at the time of driving he was not having any driving license to ride the motorcycle.
The Tribunal by considering the said aspect fixed 25% contributory negligence on the part of the appellant.

The learned counsel contends that as for as the disability is concerned, PW.2-Doctor in his evidence stated that the petitioner got permanent physical disability to an extent of 40% to right lower limb and 20% to right hand.
By considering that aspect, the Tribunal has rightly arrived at the conclusion that the functional disability of the body could be considered as 35% and loss of earning capacity as 12%.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.
9. We have bestowed our anxious consideration to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and also perused the material available on record including trial court records.

10. As could be seen from the record, the Tribunal fixed the contributory negligence on the appellant/claimant only for the reason that, the appellant was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident.
However, it is nowhere forthcoming either in the judgment or in the evidence that the appellant being the rider, of the two wheeler was driving his motor bike rashly and negligently.
Moreover, on perusal of the Ex.P.4-rough sketch of the spot of accident, it clearly depicts that the Mahendra Pick- up vehicle had strayed to the extremely southern side of the road i.e. right side.
Hence, it can be easily concluded that the said accident was caused only due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver, of the four wheeler.

In such circumstances, as per law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sri Dinesh Kumar J. @ Dinesh J (supra) in para 8 and 9 of the said judgment, the Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:

sentences.text: Insofar as the judgment of the High Court is concerned, the Division Bench has placed a considerable degree of importance on the fact that there was no visible damage to the lorry but that it was the motor cycle which had suffered damage and that there was no eye-witness.
We are in agreement with the submission which has been urged on behalf of the appellant that plea of contributory negligence was accepted purely on the basis of conjecture and without any evidence.

Once the finding that there was contributory negligence on the part of the appellant is held to be without any basis, the second aspect which weighed both with the tribunal and the High Court, that the appellant had not produced the driving licence, would be of no relevance.

This aspect has been considered in a judgment of this Court in Sudhir Kumar (supra) where it was held as follows:
"9.If a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence.
The same, by itself, in our opinion, may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
It has been held by the courts below that it was the driver of the mini truck who was driving rashly and negligently.
It is one thing to say that the appellant was not possessing any licence but no finding of fact has been arrived at that he was driving the two-wheeler rashly and - 10 - negligently.

If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how, only because he was not having a licence, he would be held to be guilty of contributory negligence..."

11. The appellant was not possessing valid driving license, he may have committed an offence but that by itself cannot be considered as a cause for the accident or that he contributed his negligence to the accident.
In the circumstances, the Tribunal has erred by holding that appellant/claimant also contributed 25% negligence to the accident.

12. Coming to the next aspect functional disability caused to the petitioner and loss of earning capacity is concerned, the Tribunal erred by taking into consideration the loss of earning capacity as 12%.

The judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sri.Anthony @ Anthony Swamy (supra)
held in paragraphs 10 and 11 as follows:
10. Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another, 2011 (1) SCC 343 lucidly sets out the principles for grant of compensation in cases of permanent physical functional disability as follows:
- 11 - "10. Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

In most of the cases, the percentage of economic loss, that is, the percentage of loss of earning capacity, arising from a permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability.

Some Tribunals wrongly assume that in all cases, a particular extent (percentage) of permanent disability would result in a corresponding loss of earning capacity, and consequently, if the evidence produced show 45% as the permanent disability, will hold that there is 45% loss of future earning capacity.

In most of the cases, equating the extent (percentage) of loss of earning capacity to the extent (percentage) of permanent disability will result in award of either too low or too high a compensation.

11. What requires to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money, to arrive at the - 12 - future loss of earnings (by applying the standard multiplier method used to determine loss of dependency).

We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that the percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation."

13. In the case on hand, though the Tribunal arrived at the conclusion that the functional disability of the body could be considered as 35% but, strangely, loss of earning capacity is considered at 12%.
Even by perusal of evidence of the PW.2 -Doctor, who examined the injured, clearly opined that the injured got permanent physical disability amounts 40% to right lower limb and 20% to right hand.
Hence, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, in our considered opinion, Tribunal also erred in considering the loss of earning capacity.
In that view of the matter, in our considered opinion the - 13 - appellant/claimant lost his earning capacity to an extent of 30%.
14. As per Lok-adalath chart, notional income for the accident of the year 2014 is Rs.7,500/-.

But,
Tribunal taken notional income at Rs.7,000/- and the same has to be modified at Rs.7,500/-.
The multiplier applicable for the case on hand would be 15.
Hence the claimant is entitled for Loss of future earning capacity at Rs.4,05,000/-.

15. Hence, the claimant is entitled for compensation as under:
1. Loss of future earning 4,05,000-00 2. Pain and suffering 50,000-00 Shri.

Medical Expenses 90,664-00 5.
Future Medical Expenses 5,000-00 5,57,664-00 16.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled for total enhanced compensation of Rs.3,29,766-00 (Rs.5,57,664 - 14 - less Rs.2,27,898-00) along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

17. Accordingly, we pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The impugned Judgment and award dated 10.10.2017 passed in MVC No.2036/2015 by the IX Additional District and Sessions Judge and Addl. MACT Belagavi is hereby modified.

iv. The respondent No.2- Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
